title: Practitioner Exam
description: 40 questions covering all five modules, drawn from a pool of 50. Pass mark is 80%. This is an open-book exam — take your time, browse any module to refresh your memory, or ask the AI assistant for help. Your answers are saved as you go, so leaving the page to look something up is fine. Explanations show after submission so you can learn from any answers you missed.

questions.scenario: A finance analyst wants to explore revenue by product line, territory, and quarter. They need to drill from a year into its quarters whenever a figure looks odd.
questions.prompt: Which tool should they build this in?
options: Report Designer
Dashboard Designer
Analyzer
Interactive Reports
questions.explanation: The **Analyzer** tool is designed for OLAP analysis: users pivot measures across dimensions and drill down through a hierarchy, such as from years to quarters, with a double-click, exploring the cube whenever a figure looks odd.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Choosing the right tool

questions.scenario: A sales director wants one page showing a geographic analysis, an existing orders report, and an inventory list, all filtered by the same Territory selection.
questions.prompt: Which tool builds this page?
options: Interactive Reports
Analyzer
Dashboard Designer
Schema Workbench
questions.explanation: The **Dashboard Designer** allows the integration of content from Analyzer, Interactive Reporting, and Report Designer into a single page using panels. It enables the application of a single dashboard prompt to bind to the parameters of each report on the page.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Choosing the right tool

questions.scenario: A regional manager needs a printable list of orders grouped by Territory and Country, with a revenue subtotal for each group and no charts.
questions.prompt: Which tool is the best fit?
options: Interactive Reports
Dashboard Designer
Pentaho Data Integration
Analyzer
questions.explanation:
Interactive Reports are designed to build **grouped tabular reports** with subtotals and specific page setup for printing from a metadata model.

This tool provides the necessary functionality to generate the structured list required for the printable report.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Choosing the right tool

questions.scenario: The database behind the Orders metadata model moves to a new server. Forty Interactive Reports are built on that model.
questions.prompt: What has to change for the reports to keep working?
options: The data source, re-selected inside each report
Nothing, since each report keeps its own copy of the rows
The saved query in each report, one at a time
Only the database connection the Orders model uses
questions.explanation:
The **database connection** belongs to the metadata model. Every report built on that model accesses the database through that specific connection, so updating the connection in the model automatically updates the access point for all associated reports.

Because reports store a query against the model rather than raw SQL against a specific server, the query does not need to be updated individually for each report.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Data governance

questions.scenario: Regional leads want an orders report in their inbox on the first of every month, and nobody wants to run it by hand.
questions.prompt: What should the report owner set up in the User Console?
options: A Favorite for each lead that points to the report
A monthly schedule for the report that emails its output
A dashboard holding the report, with a refresh interval
A copy of the report in each lead's Home folder
questions.explanation: A **monthly schedule** runs the report on the server's scheduler at a set recurrence and can email the output, which allows the report to be delivered without anyone needing to open it manually.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Schedules

questions.scenario: A modeler proposes renaming the Territory level of a sales cube to Region to match new company language. Dozens of analyses and several dashboards use the cube.
questions.prompt: What is the strongest reason to treat this as a reviewed change rather than a quick edit?
options: Mondrian must reload the fact table before the new name appears
Renaming a level resets the cube's measures to a Count aggregation
A cube cannot be republished once reports have been built on it
Saved analyses and dashboards refer to the level by its schema name
questions.explanation:
An Analyzer report saves each field as a schema formula such as `[Markets].[Territory]`, and dashboards map parameters to those levels, so a rename reaches every report and link built on the cube.

That reach is why models are **reviewed and versioned** like software.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Data governance

questions.scenario: In one company, business users build their own reports in the browser from governed models. In another, IT builds every report and business users only open them.
questions.prompt: What distinguishes the first approach from the second?
options: Whether the finished reports can be scheduled
Where the data lives, in spreadsheets or databases
Who authors the reports, not which models they use
How current the data is when a report is opened
questions.explanation: The distinction between self-service and managed reporting is based on **who authors the reports**. While both approaches can utilize the same governed models and underlying data sources, the first approach empowers business users to perform the authoring, while the second keeps authoring within the IT department.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Self-service vs managed reporting

questions.scenario: EMEA managers must see only EMEA rows and NA managers only NA rows in every report built on the Orders model, including reports written next year.
questions.prompt: Where should that restriction be defined?
options: In the repository permissions on each report's own folder
In the Orders model's security, keyed to the user's role
As a Territory prompt defaulting to the user's region
As a Territory filter saved into each report
questions.explanation: Defining the restriction in the **metadata model security** applies it to every query the model generates, so every report built on the model, now or next year, is restricted by the user's role, whichever report is opened.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Overview — Data governance

questions.scenario: Finance staff adjust the columns of an Interactive Report in the User Console every month. A developer plans to open that report in Report Designer, add a sub-report, and publish it back in its place.
questions.prompt: What should finance staff be told before the change?
options: They will no longer be able to edit it in Interactive Reports
Its metadata model will have to be replaced by a SQL query
They will be able to open it only from Report Designer
They can still edit it in Interactive Reports, minus the sub-report
questions.explanation: An Interactive Report can be opened in **Report Designer** for further customization, where charts and other elements, including sub-reports, can be added. The move is **one-way**: once a report has been customized in Report Designer, it can no longer be edited with the Interactive Reporting module in the User Console, so finance would have to stop making their monthly column changes there.
questions.source: analyst-ba-practitioner/05-interactive-reports

questions.scenario: The Orders model was built in Pentaho Metadata Editor, and analysts use it every day in Interactive Reports. When one of them starts a new Analyzer report, Orders is not in the list of data sources.
questions.prompt: Why is Orders not offered in Analyzer?
options: Analyzer reports read CSV files only, never database tables
Analyzer reports query database tables directly, without a model
Only administrators can open a metadata model in Analyzer
Analyzer reports are built on a Mondrian schema, not a metadata model
questions.explanation:
Interactive Reports and Analyzer read different kinds of data source. An Interactive Report is built on a **metadata model**, created in Pentaho Metadata Editor or generated by the Data Source Wizard, while an Analyzer report is built on a **Mondrian schema**, also called an Analysis Model: an XML model with cube-like structures over fact and dimension tables in a relational database.

Orders exists as a metadata model, so Analyzer has nothing to open until a Mondrian schema is created for the same data, in Schema Workbench or with the Data Source Wizard.
questions.source: analyst-ba-practitioner/09-analyzer-reports

questions.scenario: A new analyst has a login to the Pentaho Server and a web browser, and no software is installed on their laptop.
questions.prompt: What can they do from the User Console alone?
options: Build pixel-perfect reports as in Report Designer
Design transformations and jobs on a canvas
Open, create, and schedule reports and dashboards
Edit Mondrian schemas as in Schema Workbench
questions.explanation: The **User Console** is the web-based front end of the Pentaho Server. It provides the interface for users to open content, create Interactive Reports, create Analyzer reports, and schedule reports and dashboards.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Pentaho User Console

questions.scenario: An IT manager is choosing between giving 300 business users browser access to the User Console and installing a desktop reporting tool on each laptop.
questions.prompt: Which consideration most favors the browser?
options: Reports run faster in a browser than in any desktop reporting tool
One server upgrade reaches every user, with no clients to update
Browsers can render chart types that desktop tools cannot draw
Browser access removes the need to manage user permissions
questions.explanation: Using a browser ensures that content, permissions, and updates are hosted on the server. This means a single **server upgrade** reaches all 300 users immediately, preventing individual laptops from falling out of sync.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Pentaho User Console

questions.scenario: An analyst opens an Interactive Report a month after it was saved and sees this morning's orders in it.
questions.prompt: Why does the report show current data?
options: The server refreshes a stored copy of its rows each night
The data source copies its new rows into the report file
The report was scheduled to rebuild itself every day
The saved report holds a query definition and re-runs it
questions.explanation:
An Interactive Report is a bundle of definitions, including the layout and the query against the model, but it does not contain a stored copy of the rows. When the report is opened, it executes the **query definition** against the live data source.

Because the report refers to a live data source rather than a static file or cached result, the data is current at the time of opening.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Data sources

questions.scenario: A user opened a sales report yesterday but cannot remember which folder it is in, and wants to open it again.
questions.prompt: Where in the User Console will they find it fastest?
options: Administration
Recents
Opened
Schedules
questions.explanation: The **Recents** section lists content that the user has opened lately, allowing the user to access the report without knowing its specific folder path.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Perspectives

questions.scenario: To keep a confidential report from the Sales role, a consultant removes the link to its folder from a custom portal page but leaves the folder's permissions unchanged.
questions.prompt: Can a Sales user still open the report?
options: Yes, from any client, because the folder's permissions allow it
No, because content with no link to it cannot be requested
Only once an administrator shares the report with them again
No, because the portal page now controls access to the folder
questions.explanation:
The server checks the **access-control list** of the requested content on every request. Because the folder still grants the Sales role access, the user can still fetch the report using any client, including the User Console, Report Designer, a script, or the REST API.

Content does not require a link to be requested; any client can request a path from the server. A portal page is only one of many possible clients and does not manage permissions; only the **folder permissions** determine if a user can access the file.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Users & Roles

questions.scenario: An analyst has finished a report the whole sales team will run each week, and has a draft of another report that is not ready to share.
questions.prompt: Where should each be saved?
options: Team report in a shared Public folder, draft in their Home folder
Team report in their Home folder, draft in a shared Public folder
Both in their Home folder, with the folder shared to the sales team
Both in a shared Public folder, with the draft renamed
questions.explanation: Content in a shared **Public folder** can be found and run by others, subject to the folder's permissions, while a **Home folder** is personal space, so the draft stays private until it is ready.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: User Console — Browse Files

questions.scenario: The data warehouse is reloaded one night each month. An operations analyst must pause every user's scheduled reports before the reload and resume them afterwards, without being given access to the Administration perspective.
questions.prompt: Which operation permission should the analyst's role hold?
options: Schedule Content
Administer Security
Execute Schedules
Execute
questions.explanation:
**Execute Schedules** reaches beyond the holder's own schedules: a role that holds it can view all scheduled reports from all users, and **pause and resume** all of them. The analyst can pause every schedule before the reload starts and resume them all when it ends.

Access to the Administration perspective comes with Administer Security, which the analyst does not need.
questions.source: analyst-ba-practitioner/04-user-console-puc

questions.scenario: A sales manager opens the same three finance reports every morning, each kept in a different folder that the finance team maintains. The manager wants all three listed on the Home page and must always open the version finance last saved.
questions.prompt: What should the manager do?
options: Copy each report into the manager's Home folder
Schedule each report to run each morning
Move each report into one Public folder
Add each report to Favorites
questions.explanation:
**Favorites** is a per-user list of files that the Home page shows for quick access. A report is added to it from Browse Files with **Add to Favorites** in the File Actions pane, or with the star beside it in Recents.

Adding a Favorite writes a per-user setting, not a copy of the report, so each click opens the file the finance team maintains, with every change they have saved.
questions.source: analyst-ba-practitioner/04-user-console-puc

questions.scenario: The Sales role has read access to the Public folder. An analyst creates a Forecasts folder inside Public, saves a confidential report in it, and changes no permissions. Sales users are soon found opening the report.
questions.prompt: Why can Sales users open the report?
options: Files under Public ignore the permissions of their own folder
Their Read Content permission opens every file on the server
The new folder inherited its permissions from Public
A new folder is open to all roles until someone restricts it
questions.explanation:
Every report, dashboard, and folder in the repository is a node with its own **access-control list**, and the server checks that list on every request. A new folder's list is **inherited from its parent**, so Forecasts started with the permissions of Public, read access for Sales included, and nobody narrowed them afterwards.

Restricting the report means changing the permissions on Forecasts or on the report itself, which is done in the Browse Files perspective.
questions.source: analyst-ba-practitioner/04-user-console-puc

questions.scenario: A support team must open existing reports and schedule them, but must never add, change, or remove reports themselves. An administrator proposes giving the team the default Power User role.
questions.prompt: What is the strongest objection to this proposal?
options: It lets them create, delete, and publish content
It does not include the permission to schedule content
It lets them create, edit, and delete data sources
It lets them pause and resume every user's schedules
questions.explanation:
The default **Power User** role holds Schedule Content, Read Content, Publish Content, Create Content, and Execute. **Create Content** lets a user create, import, delete, and save reports to the repository, and **Publish Content** lets client tools store reports and data models there, so the team could change exactly what it must leave alone.

Roles can be altered to suit a need, so a role holding only Read Content and Schedule Content would let the team open and schedule reports without either of those permissions.
questions.source: analyst-ba-practitioner/04-user-console-puc

questions.scenario: An orders report with a Row Limit of 100 shows a plausible subtotal for its first territory, but later territories are missing or far too small, and no error appears.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely cause?
options: The later territories have no orders in the chosen date range.
Subtotals are computed only for the first page of output.
The summary function was set to Average instead of Sum.
The query stopped at 100 rows, so the totals cover only those.
questions.explanation:
The **Row Limit** is applied in the query, so the database returns only the first 100 rows in sort order, and the summaries add up only what arrived.

Set the Row Limit to **Maximum** before trusting a total.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Query settings

questions.scenario: A report grouped by Territory lists one row per order line, and the manager wants each territory's subtotal to show how many different orders it contains.
questions.prompt: Which summary should be set on Order Number?
options: Count Distinct
Maximum
Count
Sum
questions.explanation: The **Count Distinct** summary counts how many unique values a group holds, so an order with several lines is counted once in its territory's total.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Totals

questions.scenario: Each territory manager wants the same orders report showing only their own territory, and the author wants to maintain a single report.
questions.prompt: What should the author add to the report?
options: A calculated field that returns each manager's territory
A prompt on Territory, so the value is chosen at run time
A group on Territory, so each manager scrolls to their own
A filter on Territory, set to each manager's value in turn
questions.explanation:
A **prompt** is a filter whose value is provided at run time, so a single report serves each manager with the territory they choose.

The same report can also go into schedules and dashboards, where the parameter is set for each territory.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Prompts

questions.scenario: A wide grouped report looks fine in the browser, but when it is exported to PDF its rightmost columns spill onto separate pages.
questions.prompt: Which change fixes the exported layout?
options: Raise the Row Limit to Maximum
Export the report as CSV instead of PDF
Turn on Sticky HTML header rows
Switch to landscape in Page Setup
questions.explanation: **Page Setup** controls page format, orientation, and margins, and the default is Letter portrait. Switching to **landscape** gives the columns room on each page.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Page setup

questions.scenario: The NA and EMEA sales teams each want an orders report that differs only in territory, delivered monthly to their own recipients.
questions.prompt: Which approach is easiest to maintain?
options: One report per team, copied each month from a master
One report with a Territory prompt, one schedule per team
Two reports, each with its own territory filter fixed in it
One report grouped by Territory, sent to both teams
questions.explanation:
A report with a **Territory prompt** is a single definition of the report. Each schedule then sets the `Territory` parameter for its own team.

A change to the layout or logic is made once, in the shared report.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Orders NA and EMEA

questions.scenario: An analyst adds Customer Name, Order Date, and Total to an Interactive Report. The three fields come from three different tables in the database.
questions.prompt: How is the join between those tables worked out?
options: The analyst picks the join keys as each field is added
The database infers the join from matching column names
The metadata layer follows relationships defined in the model
Interactive Reports joins the rows together in the user's browser
questions.explanation: The **metadata layer** follows relationships established in the data model to generate a single SQL statement with the correct joins. Because the relationships are defined once in the model, the analyst does not need to specify join keys for each field, and the join is executed in the database rather than in the browser.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Metadata model

questions.scenario: An analyst adds a calculated field, `Tax = [Total] * 0.15`, to an Interactive Report. The analyst then attempts to filter for orders where the tax amount exceeds 1,000 but finds the filtering option is unavailable for that field.
questions.prompt: Why can the calculated field not be filtered?
options: The expression has to be written in SQL before it can be filtered.
Calculated fields must be published before they can be filtered.
The report engine computes it after the query has returned.
Filters accept only fields that already have a prompt.
questions.explanation:
The **reporting engine** evaluates a calculated field row by row after the data is retrieved from the database. Because the calculation occurs after the query is completed, the database cannot process a `WHERE` clause for that specific field.

To enable filtering, sorting, and aggregation on a calculation, the expression must be defined as a formula column within the **metadata model** rather than as a calculation in the report interface.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Computed fields

questions.scenario: A report is filtered to one territory, grouped by Country, and sorted by Customer Name. The author wants to understand how the rows are ordered for the groups to be processed correctly.
questions.prompt: How are the rows put in order for the groups to work?
options: The groups are formed first, and the filter is applied after
Group fields go into the query's ORDER BY ahead of the column sort
The report engine re-sorts all of the returned rows in memory by group
The column sort is applied first, and the groups follow it
questions.explanation:
The engine starts a new group when a value changes between consecutive rows, so the **group fields** go into the query's `ORDER BY` ahead of any column sort, and the database does the ordering.

The filter goes into the `WHERE` clause, so it runs in the database before any rows reach the engine.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Filtering & sorting

questions.scenario: A finance system accepts only delimited text files, and the regional director wants a fixed-layout copy of the same report to print for a board meeting.
questions.prompt: Which two export formats meet those needs?
options: CSV
PDF
Excel
HTML
PowerPoint (PPTX)
questions.explanation: The **CSV** format is a delimited text file that the finance system can load. The **PDF** format maintains a fixed page layout for printing.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Output formats

questions.scenario: A sales manager wants an orders report covering only the Motorcycles and Planes product lines, with Quantity Ordered subtotalled for each product line within each territory.
questions.prompt: Which report design meets this?
options: Filter Product Line to the two lines, then sort by Territory and then Product Line
Prompt for Product Line, then group by Territory and then Product Line
Filter Product Line to the two lines, then group by Product Line and then Territory
Filter Product Line to the two lines, then group by Territory and then Product Line
questions.explanation: The filter keeps only the two product lines, and nesting Product Line inside Territory puts a **subtotal** for each product line within each territory.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Interactive Reports — Ships and Trains

questions.scenario: A product manager is exploring a sales cube in Analyzer and wants to reshape and extend the analysis without requiring assistance from the IT department.
questions.prompt: Which two actions can they perform directly in the analysis?
options: Drill from Years down to Quarters
Add a new level to the Time hierarchy
Create a calculated measure from Sales
Rewrite the SQL that Mondrian generates
Correct order rows in the fact table
questions.explanation:
Drilling through a hierarchy and creating a **calculated measure** are analysis actions because each action modifies the report's **MDX query**.

These operations occur within the **Analyzer** tool, which reads from the cube rather than modifying the underlying data or the schema.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — OLAP & Mondrian

questions.scenario: An analyst viewing Sales by Years double-clicks the 2003 column header. The header expands into QTR1 through QTR4 while every other field remains the same.
questions.prompt: What is this operation called?
options: Drill-through
Pivot
Slice
Drill-down
questions.explanation:
The operation of moving from one level of a hierarchy to the level below it, such as from years to quarters, while keeping the rest of the view the same is called a **drill-down**.

```text
Years
  2004          double-click
    QTR1
    QTR2
    QTR3
    QTR4
```
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Drill-down

questions.scenario: A sales manager wants each cell in a Quantity column to show a bar whose length reflects its value, so the largest countries stand out without reading the numbers.
questions.prompt: Which conditional formatting should be applied to Quantity?
options: Data Bar
Trend Arrow
Color Scale
Heat grid
questions.explanation: A **Data Bar** draws a bar in each cell sized to its value, which provides a direct visual comparison by length.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Conditional formatting

questions.scenario: Management wants to see at a glance which countries in a territory account for the largest share of the quantity sold in one year.
questions.prompt: Which visualization suits this best?
options: Tree map
Line chart
Scatter chart
Heat grid
questions.explanation: A **Tree map** sizes each rectangle by its value within the whole, so the biggest contributors stand out at a glance.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Visualisations

questions.scenario: The nightly load added yesterday's orders to the sales fact table, but an analysis that had been run before the load still shows the old totals after it is refreshed.
questions.prompt: What is the most likely cause?
options: Analyzer only sends a new query when the layout changes
Mondrian is serving cell values it cached before the load
The browser is showing a cached copy of the earlier page
The saved analysis stored its results along with its layout
questions.explanation:
Mondrian keeps a **cache of cell values**, shared across users, so cells it already holds are served without new SQL.

**Administration > Clear Cache** flushes it, and the new rows appear.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Administration

questions.scenario: A cube models Country, State, and City as three separate dimensions instead of one Markets hierarchy. Users complain that double-clicking a country does not show its cities.
questions.prompt: Why does this design block the drill?
options: Analyzer supports drill-down only on the Time dimension
Cities must first be added as a filter before drilling
Drill-down works only once drill-through links have been enabled
Drill-down follows one hierarchy, and no hierarchy holds all three
questions.explanation:
A double-click requests the children of a specific member from the engine. This request succeeds only when the schema defines the levels within a single **hierarchy**, such as Country > State > City.

Because the dimensions are defined as three separate entities, there is no inherent parent-child relationship between them to support a **drill-down** operation.

```text
Markets
  Country
    State
      City
```
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Hierarchies

questions.scenario: Margin % is needed in a dozen Analyzer reports and two dashboards, and finance insists it is calculated identically everywhere.
questions.prompt: Where should Margin % be defined?
options: As a user-defined measure in each Analyzer report
As a calculated field in an Interactive Report
As a calculated member in the Mondrian schema
In a spreadsheet, after exporting the data to CSV
questions.explanation:
Defining the calculation as a **calculated member** in the Mondrian schema ensures that the definition and format are consistent across every report and dashboard that utilizes the cube.

This centralized configuration ensures that all users compute the metric identically, as the calculation is tied to the data model rather than the individual report definition.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Calculated measures

questions.scenario: A manager identifies an unexpectedly high sales figure for a specific territory, product line, and quarter. The manager wants to view the individual order lines behind that aggregated figure.
questions.prompt: What should be enabled in the analysis?
options: Drill-through links on measure cells, in Report Options
Subtotals on the Territory level, with Show Subtotals
A Rank user-defined measure on the Sales column
Drill-down on the Quarters level of the Time hierarchy
questions.explanation: Enabling **drill-through links** on measure cells in Report Options turns each non-calculated measure into a link that opens the fact rows behind that aggregate value.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Drill-through

questions.scenario: An analysis filtered to three EMEA countries shows a Territory subtotal set to Aggregate. A colleague expected it to match the cube's full EMEA figure, but the value is lower.
questions.prompt: Why is the subtotal lower than the full EMEA figure?
options: Totals are visual by default, covering only members left after filters
Subtotals leave out every member whose value is blank rather than zero
Aggregate averages the visible cells instead of adding them all together
The cube caches EMEA figures only at the country level of the hierarchy
questions.explanation:
By default, the Analyzer uses **visual totals**. The **Aggregate** calculation is performed only on the members remaining after a filter is applied.

To include the values of the members that were filtered out and return the full figure, the user must select the **Display Totals that Includes Filtered Out Values** option.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — Totals

questions.scenario: An analyst drags Territory to rows and Years to columns, and an administrator then opens the analysis log to see what ran.
questions.prompt: What does the log show that Analyzer sent to Mondrian?
options: A request to reload the cube from its tables
An MDX query, which Mondrian turned into SQL
A SQL query that Analyzer wrote directly
An MQL query against a metadata model
questions.explanation: Analyzer uses **MDX** as its underlying language. Every interaction in the interface translates into an MDX query sent to the Mondrian engine, which then handles the conversion to SQL to query the fact and dimension tables. The analysis log records this **MDX query** and the time it took to execute.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Analyzer Reports — OLAP & Mondrian

questions.scenario: A designer is building a sales dashboard and wants to combine existing content with new visuals in its panels.
questions.prompt: Which three of these can be placed in a panel?
options: A PDI transformation canvas
An Analyzer report from the repository
A web page, shown by its URL
A Mondrian schema, opened for editing
A chart built in Chart Designer
questions.explanation:
A **dashboard panel** can display Interactive Reporting, Analyzer, and Report Designer content from the repository, as well as data tables, charts built in Chart Designer, and any web page via its URL.

These components provide a variety of ways to visualize and interact with data within the dashboard interface.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Overview

questions.scenario: A designer adds a Territory prompt to a dashboard, but the orders report in one panel offers no parameter to associate it with, so the report ignores the selection.
questions.prompt: What must change for the prompt to filter that report?
options: The panel must have content linking enabled on its Territory field
The prompt must take its values from a Metadata List
The dashboard must be saved before the prompt can apply
The report's Territory filter must be defined as a parameter
questions.explanation: A dashboard prompt can be applied to a report only when the report's filter is set up as a **parameter**, which the prompt's value is then mapped onto.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Filters & content linking

questions.scenario: A dashboard chart is meant to compare only the product lines beginning with M, but its query returns every row of a large inventory table, and the panel loads slowly.
questions.prompt: Which change will do most to speed it up?
options: Add a Product Line condition to the chart's query
Switch the dashboard to a lighter visual theme
Give the chart a larger panel in the layout
Set a shorter refresh interval on the dashboard
questions.explanation:
A condition added to the query becomes a SQL `WHERE` clause, so the database returns only the rows the chart needs.

Filtering at the query level cuts the **data volume** sent from the database to the dashboard.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Inventory

questions.scenario: A team needs a quick inventory table on a dashboard, and no report currently exists for it. A colleague suggests building and publishing an Interactive Report first to place in the panel.
questions.prompt: What is the more direct option?
options: Insert a Data Table panel that queries the inventory model
Insert a URL panel that points straight at the inventory database
Wait for IT to publish a report built in Report Designer
Export the inventory to CSV and place the file in a panel
questions.explanation: The **Data Table panel** queries a data source directly, so the table goes on the dashboard with no report to build and publish first.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Inventory

questions.scenario: In a three-panel dashboard, clicking a product in an Analyzer report updates a pie chart of territory sales, and clicking a territory in the pie updates a bar chart of order status for that product and territory.
questions.prompt: Which panels re-run their queries when a user clicks a territory in the pie chart?
options: Only the bar chart
The pie chart and the bar chart
All three, starting with the report
None, until the dashboard is refreshed
questions.explanation:
The bar chart is the only panel that takes its territory from the pie chart. When a user interacts with the pie chart, the **content linking** logic triggers a query refresh only for the downstream component.

The pie chart publishes a value rather than subscribing to a new one, and the Analyzer report does not have any active subscriptions, so neither of those components re-queries upon a click.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Product Performance

questions.scenario: A designer enables content linking on the Product field of an Analyzer panel, but no other panel changes yet when a product is clicked.
questions.prompt: What has enabling content linking done so far?
options: Made the panel publish the clicked product as a parameter
Added a Product prompt to the dashboard's prompt toolbar
Filtered every panel on the dashboard by the product
Linked the panel to every chart that has a Product column
questions.explanation: Enabling content linking declares an **output parameter** that the panel emits on each click. Nothing reacts until another panel maps one of its parameters to that output.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Content linking

questions.scenario: Managers using a sales dashboard must be able to pick one or more territories with a single click each, and the list must stay in step with the data as territories are added.
questions.prompt: Which prompt set-up meets both needs?
options: Text field, values typed in by the user, multiple selections allowed
Buttons, values from a static list, one selection only
Buttons, values from a Metadata List, multiple selections allowed
Drop-down, values from a Metadata List, one selection only
questions.explanation: The use of **Buttons** allows a manager to select an option with a single click, while a **Metadata List** dynamically queries the system to ensure the list remains current as new territories are added. Enabling **multiple selections** ensures that more than one territory can be chosen simultaneously.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Vendor Sales

questions.scenario: A dashboard requires one panel showing each territory's share of total sales and another showing how monthly sales have moved over two years.
questions.prompt: Which pair of Chart Designer chart types fits best?
options: A pie chart for the share, a dial chart for the trend
A pie chart for the share, a line chart for the trend
A dial chart for the share, a pie chart for the trend
A line chart for the share, a pie chart for the trend
questions.explanation:
A **pie chart** effectively represents parts of a whole, making it suitable for displaying the proportion of total sales contributed by each territory.

A **line chart** is designed to show changes over an ordered time axis, making it the appropriate choice for visualizing a trend over multiple months.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Chart selection

questions.scenario: A chart's query has the condition `Product Name = {PRODUCT}` with a default value, and `PRODUCT` is mapped to clicks in another panel.
questions.prompt: What does the chart show when the dashboard first opens, before anyone clicks?
options: Every product's figures, until a product is clicked
Figures for the default product, until a click replaces it
An error, because PRODUCT does not have a value yet
An empty chart, until a product has been clicked
questions.explanation:
The **default value** assigned to the parameter ensures that the query has a valid input immediately upon loading. This means the chart displays data for the specific product defined in the default until a user interaction updates the variable.

Because the condition is explicitly defined, the query always has a value to process, preventing the chart from appearing empty or triggering an error during the initial load.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Product Performance

questions.scenario: A designer maps a chart's PRODUCT parameter to an Analyzer panel's Product output. They click a product in the not-yet-saved dashboard, but the chart does not change.
questions.prompt: What should they do first?
options: Add a Product prompt to the prompt toolbar
Enable drill-through links in the Analyzer report
Save the dashboard, then test the link again
Rebuild the chart's query against the cube
questions.explanation: Content linking only functions once the dashboard has been **saved**. An unsaved dashboard will ignore a click even if the parameter mapping is correct.
questions.source: Pentaho Analyst - Practitioner: Dashboard Designer — Content linking
